scenarios.reason: Describes the Claude skill workflow that writes the user guide, not application behaviour. There is no app code path to assert; the guide's own traceability footers and status mode are the check.

scenarios.scenario: saldo/Same saldo regardless of runtime timezone
scenarios.reason: Comparing two runtime timezones needs two processes: Node caches the zone at startup, so a runtime TZ change has no effect. The suite is instead parameterized by TZ (jest.config.mjs pins a non-UTC zone; TZ=UTC npm run test:ci runs it again), and 'Begin date at the UTC day boundary' covers the mechanism that makes the result invariant.

scenarios.scenario: data-load-performance/Layout and page read the same data
scenarios.reason: React's per-request cache() only dedupes inside a real request scope. The Jest harness mocks cache() to an identity function so server modules can load under jsdom, so request-scoped memoization cannot be observed there.
Requires two separate request scopes to observe that memoization does not leak between them. Jest has no request boundary, and the e2e layer cannot see per-request query counts.

scenarios.scenario: statistics/Same grouping regardless of runtime timezone
scenarios.reason: Comparing two runtime timezones needs two processes: Node caches the zone at startup. The suite is parameterized by TZ instead (jest.config.mjs pins a non-UTC zone; TZ=UTC npm run test:ci runs it again), and 'Worklog near UTC midnight' asserts the UTC grouping that makes the figures invariant.

The requirement itself states this is enforced by code review, not tooling: no check can tell whether a test really asserts the scenario's THEN. The rule is written into CLAUDE.md and e2e/README.md, and the generated map puts each claim in the diff a reviewer reads.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/OAuth sign-in
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: Completing a Google or GitHub sign-in means driving a third-party authorization server from the browser. Stubbing it would leave the test asserting the stub rather than the provider wiring, which is the only part this requirement is about.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/JWT session with user id
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The numeric id on the session token has no representation on screen. Every authenticated page in the e2e suite depends on it to load the right user's data, but no assertion can distinguish "the id is on the session" from "the page rendered", so a browser test would not be evidence for this requirement.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/Server-side auth gate
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The gate is only observable from an unauthenticated request, and the whole Playwright suite runs behind one shared signed-in storage state. Exercising it needs a second project with no storage state, set up and reset independently — deliberately out of scope, since auth journeys are covered in Jest.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/First sign-in provisions user and seeds settings
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The scenario is about signing in a second time and finding existing settings untouched, which needs a sign-out and a fresh sign-in the shared authenticated context does not allow. The settings suite does assert that the signed-in user already has a seeded row to edit.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/Sign-up with validated credentials
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: Sign-up needs an unauthenticated context and creates a second user that the per-test reset (scoped to the single e2e user) would leave behind. Both are solvable, and both were ruled out with the rest of the auth journeys.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/Forgot-password does not reveal account existence
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The requirement is that a reset email is sent for a known address and silently not sent for an unknown one. Proving either half from the browser needs a mail transport to observe, which the e2e stack does not run.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: auth/Reset password with a valid token
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The raw token only ever reaches the user by email, so a browser test would have to read it out of the database and visit the reset link by hand — and then do it from an unauthenticated context. Left to Jest with the other auth journeys.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: data-load-performance/Independent reads execute concurrently
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: A requirement about how queries are dispatched and how many connections the pool allows. Latencies overlapping rather than summing is not visible in the DOM, and timing a page load would measure the machine, not the behaviour.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: data-load-performance/Connection attempts fail fast
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: A pool configuration fact: the acquisition timeout is set. Observing it would mean making the database refuse connections mid-suite, and the outcome is an error in the server log rather than anything the browser can assert.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: data-load-performance/Server request duration guards against premature termination
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The guard is a route-segment duration declaration read by the hosting platform. It has no runtime behaviour to drive locally — the e2e server never enforces a platform timeout.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: data-load-performance/Repeated holiday lookups over a date range are cached
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The requirement is a call-count property of the holiday cache: each year resolved once and reused. Only instrumentation can see it; the rendered saldo is identical either way, which is the point of a cache.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: saldo/Running balance from begin date
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: The worked example fixes both the begin date and the current date, and the e2e server runs on the real clock — page.clock reaches only the browser. The rest of the capability is covered end to end by comparing two begin dates, but a single named total cannot be asserted without owning the clock.

requirementsWithoutE2e.requirement: saldo/Saldo calculation is timezone-independent
requirementsWithoutE2e.reason: Comparing two runtime timezones needs two processes: Node caches the zone at startup. The Jest suite is parameterized by TZ instead (jest.config.mjs pins a non-UTC zone, TZ=UTC npm run test:ci runs it again), which is the only way to actually vary the input this requirement is about.
